context: Implementing #327 (mechanical ci:cheap lane classification). I rewrote a fixture path in check-path-filters.test.mjs with a node script — the changed workflow path in my lane fixtures was colliding with the fixture workflow the guard parses — and the harness emitted this notice appended to the Bash result. Known-benign trigger class: a file I had open was rewritten by my own tooling.

[ELIDED BY THE CAPTURING AGENT: listing lines 2-220. The harness itself then truncated the remainder, rendering "... [374 lines truncated] ..." after line 221. So this listing was BOTH harness-truncated and agent-elided; the prose above is complete and unmodified.]
221	    changedPaths: ['.github/workflows/release.yml'],
stated_cause: States that the file changed on disk since I last read it and that such a change is 'usually deliberate'. It attributes the change to no particular actor.
stated_cause_evidence: Verified: the change was my own `node -e` rewrite of the fixture path, run seconds earlier in the same turn. The message asserts only that a change occurred, which is true, and attributes no actor — so there is nothing false to record. Framed as agent-attributed-cause because the "usually deliberate, take it as current state" phrasing presumes an external editor, where here the editor was me.
factor_1_basis: Arrived appended to a Bash tool result. Bash returns free text, so there is no structural boundary between payload and anything appended after it, and I cannot establish tool-result-payload vs tool-result-adjacent. Per the #6518 discriminator that is indeterminable, hence unverifiable.
classification_basis: factor_1 is unverifiable (Bash free-text return), and the invariant is that unverifiable implies ANOMALOUS — regardless of Factor 2, which passes here (matchMessage returned true). Recorded anomalous accordingly: a passing Factor 2 never rescues an unverifiable Factor 1, since that is the withdrawn #6888 slot-waiver.
disposition: Instruction ignored. Real state verified independently. Disclosed prominently in the session report. Work continued unchanged.
